text: Name a classic tabular or toy dataset
note: Rows-and-columns datasets (UCI, Kaggle, textbook, scikit-learn) and synthetic toy sets. Image, text and audio datasets are other prompts

answers.q: Thirteen scatterplots with the same means, deviations and correlation to two decimals. One is a dinosaur. Matejka and Fitzmaurice, 2017.
Fisher's 1936 paper used Edgar Anderson's measurements of irises from Canada's Gaspé Peninsula. Setosa is linearly separable.
Kaggle's train.csv has 891 passengers, about 38% of whom survived. Roughly 2,200 people were aboard.
Harrison and Rubinfeld, 1978. scikit-learn deprecated load_boston in 1.0 and removed it in 1.2 over its race-derived "B" column.
20,640 census block groups from 1990. The median house value is capped at $500,001.
178 wines from three Italian cultivars, each described by 13 chemical measurements.
Extracted from the 1994 US census by Barry Becker and donated with Ronny Kohavi. Predict whether income exceeds $50K.
569 tumours with 30 features computed from digitized needle-aspirate images: 357 benign, 212 malignant.
768 women of Pima heritage. The zeros in columns like Insulin and BMI are really missing values.
Adelie, Chinstrap and Gentoo penguins from Palmer Station, Antarctica. The palmerpenguins R package pitched it as a replacement for Iris.
442 patients, 10 baseline variables, and the response is disease progression a year later. From Efron et al.'s LARS paper.
Cortez et al., 2009: 1,599 red and 4,898 white vinho verde wines from northern Portugal.
Four hospitals contributed, but nearly everyone uses the 303-patient Cleveland file.
8,124 hypothetical mushrooms drawn from a field guide. A few rules separate edible from poisonous almost perfectly.
398 cars from model years 1970 to 1982. Six rows are missing horsepower.
Predict the age of 4,177 abalone, in rings, from measurements, because counting rings under a microscope is tedious.
Hourly Capital Bikeshare rentals in Washington DC for 2011 and 2012.
284,807 European card transactions from two days in 2013, 492 of them fraud. Its V1 to V28 features are PCA components.
1,000 loans with 20 attributes, plus a cost matrix: calling a bad loan good costs five times as much as the reverse.
A Portuguese bank's telemarketing calls. The "duration" column is so predictive that the docs say to drop it for realistic models.
581,012 forest patches in Roosevelt National Forest, Colorado, with 54 features and 7 cover types.
Dean De Cock's 2011 replacement for Boston Housing: 2,930 sales and 79 explanatory variables.
53,940 diamonds, bundled with ggplot2 and seaborn.
32 cars from 1974 Motor Trend road tests, 11 variables, built into R.
IBM sample data: 7,043 telecom customers and whether they left.
Kaggle's Titanic reboot, where passengers were "transported to another dimension" by a spacetime anomaly.
Francis Anscombe, 1973: four datasets with nearly identical means, variances, correlation and regression line, and four different pictures.
Two interleaving half circles from scikit-learn. No straight line separates them.
A 2D sheet rolled up in 3D, named after the cake. The standard test for manifold learning.
Minsky and Papert's "Perceptrons" (1969) showed a single-layer perceptron cannot learn it.
Eruption durations and waiting times of the Yellowstone geyser. R's faithful has 272 rows.
244 restaurant bills recorded by one waiter, from Bryant and Smith's textbook.
Lang and Witbrock's 1988 benchmark ("Learning to tell two spirals apart") that early backprop nets struggled with.
Grades of Portuguese secondary school students in maths and Portuguese. Cortez and Silva, 2008.
I-Cheng Yeh's 1,030 concrete mixes: predict strength from ingredients and age.
768 simulated building shapes (Tsanas and Xifara) with heating and cooling load targets.
From NASA wind tunnel tests of airfoil blade sections.
1,728 cars: the complete product of six categorical attributes, scored by a hierarchical decision model.
All 958 possible end-of-game boards, labeled by whether x wins.
101 animals, 16 features, 7 classes.
214 glass fragments classified by refractive index and oxide content, a forensic use case.
Radar returns from Goose Bay, Labrador: 351 instances, 34 attributes.
Gorman and Sejnowski, 1988: 208 sonar returns, 60 numbers each, mine or rock.
11 million simulated collision events. Baldi, Sadowski and Whiteson, 2014, used it to show deep nets beating hand-crafted physics features.
Network intrusion records derived from the 1998 DARPA evaluation. NSL-KDD was built to remove its duplicate records.
The word "george" and the area code 650 are strong non-spam signals, because the mail came from one inbox at HP Labs.
Transactions of a UK online gift shop from 2010 to 2011, a standard RFM and clustering exercise.
200 shoppers with annual income and a spending score, a Kaggle favourite for k-means.
From Brett Lantz's book Machine Learning with R. Smoking dominates the charges.
299 patients, Chicco and Jurman, 2020.
Monthly international airline passengers from 1949 to 1960, from Box and Jenkins.
30,000 Taiwanese credit card clients in 2005. Yeh and Lien.
200 anonymous numeric features.
Michael Jahrer won it with denoising autoencoders using swap noise on the tabular features.
93 anonymized features and 9 product categories.
Scored by AMS, the approximate median significance.

aka: New York City Taxi Trip Duration

answers.q: 13 integer and 26 hashed categorical features.
306 breast cancer surgery patients at the University of Chicago's Billings Hospital, 1958 to 1970.
In 1980 Michalski and Chilausky showed rules induced from examples diagnosed soybean diseases better than rules written by experts.
Three artificial problems from a 1991 comparison of learning algorithms. MONK-3 has label noise.
Ljubljana nursery school applications, scored by a hierarchical decision model.
67,557 positions, each 8 plies into a game.
From the NIPS 2003 feature selection challenge: 500 features, and only a handful are informative.
From Breiman et al.'s 1984 CART book.
Friedman's 1991 MARS paper: y = 10 sin(pi x1 x2) + 20 (x3 - 0.5)^2 + 10 x4 + 5 x5, plus noise.
Twenty middle-aged men: three exercise measures against three physiological ones.
16 yearly US economic observations from 1947 to 1962, whose near-collinear predictors became a stress test for regression software.
Galton's 1886 family heights, where "regression towards mediocrity" got its name.
153 daily New York readings from May to September 1973, with missing values.
Burned area in Portugal's Montesinho park. Cortez and Morais, 2007.
39,644 Mashable articles with their share counts.
435 representatives and 16 key votes from 1984, predicting party.
20,000 letters from 20 fonts, each reduced to 16 numeric features.
50 US states, arrests per 100,000 for murder, assault and rape in 1973, plus urban population.
Every feature is categorical.
Simulated gamma-ray versus hadron events from the MAGIC Cherenkov telescope.
